newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian interests protected at WTO - government.
newsitem.headline: Indian interests protected at WTO - government.

text.p: The Indian government on Monday defended itself against charges it had bowed to Western pressure at world trade talks, telling parliament other countries seeking new mandates had ended up backtracking.

Commerce Minister Bolla Buli Ramaiah told the lower house of parliament, "our national interests have been fully safeguarded at the Singapore ministerial conference". He was referring to last week's meeting of the World Trade Organisation.

Last week communists, who back Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's coalition government, as well as opposition Hindu nationalists, accused the government of retreating under pressure at Singapore over labour standards and investment.
Ramaiah said in a written statement given to the lower house that India had largely won its way in both areas.

"It will be seen that it was not India which compromised its stand in any manner vis-a-vis its core interests but the other countries which had been seeking new mandates in the areas of investment and core labour standards," he said.
The commerce minister said those countries, which he did not name, "had to very substantially moderate their position in the face of stiff opposition put forward by India and some other countries".
